items.title: Critical Arbitrary File Upload Vulnerability Patched in Elementor Pro WordPress Plugin
items.summary:
On July 24th, 2026, we received a submission for an Unauthenticated Arbitrary File Upload vulnerability in Elementor Pro, a WordPress plugin with an estimated 6,000,000 active installations. This vulnerability makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to upload arbitrary files, including executable PHP files, to a vulnerable site, which can lead to remote code execution and complete site takeover.

The post Critical Arbitrary File Upload Vulnerability Patched in Elementor Pro WordPress Plugin appeared first on Wordfence.

items.title: 40,000 WordPress Sites affected by Authentication Bypass Vulnerability in User Profile Builder WordPress Plugin
items.summary:
On July 14th, 2026, we received a submission for an Authentication Bypass vulnerability in User Profile Builder, a WordPress plugin with more than 40,000 active installations. This vulnerability makes it possible for unauthenticated attackers to log in as the user with ID 1, which is typically the site administrator, resulting in full administrative takeover of the site. The vulnerability is only exploitable on sites where the plugin’s Automatically Log In setting is enabled.

The post 40,000 WordPress Sites affected by Authentication Bypass Vulnerability in User Profile Builder WordPress Plugin appeared first on Wordfence.
